items.your_version: The attachment theory part comes from my own experience and from reading I’ve done. Sex turns on bonding chemistry in our brain (like oxytocin, dopamine, vasopressin) that usually helps us form attachments, so that we don't just abandon our children.

People call oxytocin the “love hormone,” as if getting more attached should make you feel closer and safer. And if closeness was safe when you were little, maybe it does feel a bit like coming home, but if you were neglected, abused, or if your mom or dad or closest people disappeared on you, then you might deep down disbelieve that you're worthy of anyone staying with you. And then you can get more attached *and* more freaked out or suspicious about them leaving, and you might even go into flight or flight mode.

Romance Shouldn’t Be Adjudicated

But in some sense, being the one who's supposed to be more childish can be even harder than having the more responsible gender role. She may worry that I don’t find her young and beautiful enough, or that she’s too emotional, difficult, and needy. Then she can over-correct, pulling back into needing nobody, and make receiving care or letting her man lead feel like weakness.

Toft says that after fifty years he still tells his wife she’s beautiful, including finding new kinds of beauty as she ages. 

Anami talks a lot about women needing to learn to receive a man's help, leadership, or attempts at giving her pleasure, without feeling like it costs them their agency. Sometimes that’s as ordinary as a woman who knows perfectly well how to drive asking me to drive, because she likes how it feels not to. 

As her man, I can help her come into her femininity by, for example, asking, “Honey, how do you see this intuitively?” And that's actually one of the powerful sides of femininity, so it can be a good bridge also if she's a bit stuck in masculine mode. And then she might ask me to help think through the practical side to life me up and help me shine.

That's the way we can invite each other to play our unique roles rather than huff and puff in disappointment. Would you rather go to a party where you were invited or a war you got drafted into?

When a woman doesn’t know how to gently invite a man to lead, she may manufacture a crisis until the man is forced to take charge to get the same outward result.

Unfortunately, I’ve seen a lot of the latter.
